record.paper_title: A General Framework for Coloring Problems: Old Results, New Results, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Radio labeling variants on interval graphs
record.original_question: For interval graphs, determine the computational complexity of each of the following radio labeling variants: RL, where all vertices must receive distinct positive-integer labels and adjacent vertices must differ by at least 2 while minimizing span; p-RL(l), where a fixed number l of vertices are pre-labeled and the labeling must extend those values; and p-RL(*), where the number of pre-labeled vertices is part of the input.

evidence.quote: The complexity of any of the variants of Radio Labeling (RL, p-RL(l) and p-RL(*)) for interval graphs are open problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An interval graph is the intersection graph of a family of intervals on the real line: each vertex corresponds to an interval, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding intervals intersect.

A radio labeling of a graph G=(V,E) is an injective function f: V → ℤ_{>0} assigning distinct positive integers to the vertices such that |f(u) − f(v)| ≥ 2 whenever uv ∈ E. The span of f is max_{v∈V} f(v). The Radio Labeling problem (RL) asks for a radio labeling of G of minimum span.

Two pre-labeled variants are considered:
• p-RL(l): for a fixed positive integer l (not part of the input), the input consists of a graph G, a set S ⊆ V with |S| = l, and an assignment g: S → ℤ_{>0}; the task is to determine a radio labeling f of G of minimum span such that f(v) = g(v) for all v ∈ S.
• p-RL(*): the same task as p-RL(l), except that the size of the pre-labeled set S is part of the input.

Problem: Determine the computational complexity of RL, p-RL(l), and p-RL(*) when the input graph G is restricted to the class of interval graphs.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search finds general complexity results for radio labeling variants — p-RL(*) is NP-hard on cographs and on k-colorable graphs (k≥3) with a given coloring, while polynomial-time algorithms exist for bounded-degree graphs and for p-RL(l) on k-colored graphs — but no source was found establishing the complexity of RL, p-RL(l), or p-RL(*) specifically on interval graphs. The status on interval graphs therefore appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Radio Labeling with Preassigned Frequencies
status_evidence.snippet: p-RL(*) is NP-hard for cographs and for k-colorable graphs with a given k-coloring (k≥3); polynomial-time algorithms exist for bounded-degree graphs and for p-RL(l) on k-colored graphs.
status_evidence.claim: General complexity results for p-RL variants are known, but interval graphs are not addressed in these results.

status_evidence.title: Radio Labeling with Pre-assigned Frequencies
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces p-RL(l) and p-RL(*) variants and provides complexity and approximation results for several graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: The pre-labeled radio labeling variants have been studied for various graph classes, with no specific resolution for interval graphs found.
